messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGE: High latency detected for customer 'Paladin Finance' (vpc: paladin-eu-west-1). p95 baseline ~1.1s -> now ~3.2s, p99 baseline ~2.0s -> now ~18s. Affected pool: dedicated-paladin-01. Auto-pager sent to lex i. metrics: https://metrics.redwood.internal/d/paladin/pool/dedicated-paladin-01

lexi: ack — oncall here, joining. what's the customer impact? @julia can you confirm?

julia: cs update - Paladin reporting checkout timeouts, ~40% request failures on their production traffic. Their SRE is on the line, asked for ETA asap. They're labeling this critical for merchant flows.

samir: looking at traces and runtime metrics. root cause looks like KV cache thrash after a tenant-initiated long-running eval. spike started ~4471234520. seeing kv-cache-miss rate spike and GPU queue depth at 95%. backend latencies show long tail on initial token init.

maya: grabbing logs now, tail shows repeated `Failed to allocate KV cache entries` and repeated OOM-ish behaviour on runtime shards. `gpu-queue-length: 78` on node 3.

carl: propose immediate mitigations: (A) tenant-level concurrency cap for offending tenant tid-7f3, (B) add warm spare GPUs to pool, (C) route new sessions away while we stabilize. If needed we'll evict long-running sessions.

carl: mitigation commands prepared:
```
# cap tenant concurrency
redwoodctl tenant set-concurrency --tenant tid-7f3 --max-concurrency 6
# scale pool by 2 GPUs
redwoodctl pool scale --pool dedicated-paladin-01 --add-gpus 2
# set routing weights to prefer warm spare
redwoodctl routing set --pool dedicated-paladin-01 --weight 30 --fallback dedicated-paladin-warm
```

lexi: applying step 1 (tenant cap) now.

lexi: `> redwoodctl tenant set-concurrency --tenant tid-7f3 --max-concurrency 6` -> OK

samir: starting step 2 (scale warm spare).

samir: `> redwoodctl pool scale --pool dedicated-paladin-01 --add-gpus 2` -> accepted, job paladin-scale-4471234567, ETA ~90s

incident-bot: Job paladin-scale-4471234567 started by samir — monitor at https://deploys.redwood.internal/jobs/paladin-scale-4471234567

julia: I told Paladin we're applying mitigations and will follow up in 10m. they're asking for a conservative ETA and if we can avoid a full restart.

lexi: dashboards — p99 dropped from ~18s -> ~9s after tenant cap, p95 moved from ~3.2s -> ~1.6s. still above their SLO (p95=1.0s). keeping bridge open and watching. created PD P0 PD-8931 for tracking.

maya: checking recent config changes for pool: no recent config merges in last 24h, but a tenant-side job launch aligns with start. pulling full alloc logs for node 3.

carl: preparing eviction as fallback if scale/config don't settle: `redwoodctl tenant evict-sessions --tenant tid-7f3 --grace 30s` — will warn customer before evict.

lexi: scale job completed; GPUs added to pool. monitoring after scale — p99 now ~2.3s, p95 ~1.05s. trending toward SLO.

samir: propose temporary KV cache increase for pool while investigating thrash: `redwoodctl pool set-config --pool dedicated-paladin-01 --kv-cache-size 8g`

lexi: applying config now. `> redwoodctl pool set-config --pool dedicated-paladin-01 --kv-cache-size 8g` -> OK, rolling non-disruptive restart of 2 nodes.

julia: Paladin says errors dropped substantially, they see checkout success improving. I'll update their exec and ask for logs from their side about long-running jobs.

lexi: handoff note: I'm oncall until 02:00 UTC. if this regresses, page carl (next oncall). created a follow-up doc: confluence.redwood/internal/paladin-slo-incident-4471234567, and RCA ticket IN-447123.

carl: acknowledged, will monitor overnight and review KV eviction heuristics tomorrow AM.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigations applied. Customer-facing errors reduced. Severity downgraded P0 -> P1 and moved to monitoring. Bridge may be closed when stable for 20m.

lexi: holding for 20m window. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
